questions.q: Why is EUV lithography done at 13.5 nm rather than some other short wavelength?
options: 13.5 nm is the shortest wavelength any laser can produce at useful power
Mo/Si multilayer Bragg mirrors have their reflectance peak (~67-70%) near 13.5 nm and highly charged tin ions emit strongly in that band
Fused silica lenses become transparent again below 14 nm
13.5 nm is exactly one fourteenth of 193 nm, which keeps the 4x reduction optics compatible with DUV reticles
questions.explanation: No material transmits EUV, so the optics must be reflective; the only high-reflectance normal-incidence mirror is a Mo/Si multilayer whose Bragg peak sits near 13.5 nm, and the Sn8+ to Sn14+ unresolved transition array happens to radiate efficiently there.

questions.q: An NXE source has 11 reflections between the intermediate focus and the wafer, each at about 67% reflectance. Roughly what fraction of the in-band light at the IF reaches the wafer?
options: About 67%, since only the weakest mirror matters
About 30%
About 1-2%
About 0.01%
questions.explanation: 0.67 raised to the 11th power is about 0.012, so only ~1-2% of the light survives (less with a pellicle), which is why a 500 W source delivers only a few watts to the wafer and why every mirror is counted.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the pre-pulse in the LPP source?
options: It ionizes the tin to Sn8+ so the main pulse only has to heat it
It flattens the ~27 um droplet into a disk or mist a few hundred micrometers across, so the CO2 main pulse is absorbed efficiently instead of reflecting off a small dense sphere
It cleans tin off the collector between main pulses
It synchronizes the droplet generator's piezo actuator with the laser
questions.explanation: The droplet is smaller than the 10.6 um focal spot and acts as a mirror; the low-energy pre-pulse expands it into a low-density, spot-sized target 1-3 us before the main pulse, raising conversion efficiency from ~2% to ~5-6%.

questions.q: A 13.5 nm photon carries ~92 eV. At a dose of 30 mJ/cm2, roughly how many photons are incident per square nanometer of resist, and why does this matter?
options: About 20 photons/nm2; the small count makes photon shot noise a first-order cause of stochastic defects such as missing contacts
About 2,000 photons/nm2; the high count makes EUV resists heat up and outgas
About 290 photons/nm2, the same as ArF, so stochastics are no worse than DUV
About 0.2 photons/nm2, so most features receive no photons at all
questions.explanation: 30 mJ/cm2 is 3e-16 J/nm2 and one photon is 1.47e-17 J, giving ~20 photons/nm2 incident (only ~3 absorbed in a 30 nm CAR); a 16 nm edge pixel is decided by a few hundred photons, so Poisson noise of several percent is unavoidable.

questions.q: Why are the High-NA (0.55) EXE projection optics anamorphic, with 8x reduction in one direction and 4x in the other?
options: To double throughput by exposing two fields at once
Because Zeiss could not polish a rotationally symmetric mirror larger than 500 mm

Because at 4x and NA 0.55 the reticle-side cone (about +/- 8 degrees) would exceed the 6 degree chief ray angle, so the reflected and incident beams would overlap and absorber shadowing would be intolerable; 8x in the scan direction fixes this while 4x in the other keeps a usable 26 x 16.5 mm half-field
Because EUV reticles are rectangular rather than square
questions.explanation: Reticle-side NA is wafer NA divided by reduction; halving it in one direction only solves the angular overlap and mask 3D problem without quartering the field, at the cost of a half-field that forces stitching or chiplet splits for reticle-limited dies.

questions.q: Why is the source vessel back-filled with hydrogen at roughly 1 mbar instead of being kept at the hardest vacuum possible?
options: Hydrogen cools the CO2 laser amplifiers
Hydrogen raises the plasma's conversion efficiency by adding electrons
Hydrogen slows tin ions before they sputter the collector, and hydrogen radicals convert deposited tin into gaseous stannane (SnH4) that the pumps remove, while absorbing very little 13.5 nm light
Hydrogen prevents the tin droplets from freezing in flight
questions.explanation: Debris mitigation is the central reliability problem of the LPP source; H2 is the least EUV-absorbing gas, thermalizes the fast ions, and chemically etches tin off the collector as SnH4, extending collector life from weeks to many months.

questions.q: At fixed wavelength and process factor, increasing numerical aperture from 0.33 to 0.55 changes the characteristic resolution by what factor?
options: It becomes 0.33/0.55 ≈ 0.60 of its previous value
It becomes 0.55/0.33 ≈ 1.67 times larger
It is unchanged
It improves by exactly 14 times
questions.explanation: Resolution scales inversely with numerical aperture. Smaller features are possible, but depth of focus also shrinks and other process constraints remain.

questions.q: Why should two EUV throughput specifications be compared at the same exposure dose?
options: Dose determines wafer diameter
A higher required dose generally increases the light delivery time, so different-dose throughput figures are not directly comparable
Dose has no influence on exposure
All tools run at identical throughput regardless of resist
questions.explanation: The resist needs a certain energy per area. More dose demands more exposure time unless source power or another part of the system compensates; overhead also matters.
